Know the source and its owner.

  1. Machine observationsDeterministic fictional samples; asset, UTC time, unit and quality. Maintenance owns review and the purchasing handoff.
  2. Governed purchasing journalExplicit commands replay request, approval, receipt, invoice and settlement. Finance owns coding policy; named roles own decisions.
  3. Read-only analytical projectionDeclared grains, stable IDs and integer cents. One validated journal supplies the figures and source evidence.

Machine signals link to a request through a reviewed case; they do not directly create expenses or prove completed work. Work completion has its own technician record and independent verification.

Import without changing what the records mean
  1. If you choose to use an external spreadsheet or BI tool, import with UTF-8, a comma delimiter and automatic type detection off.
  2. Keep identifiers as Text. The schema lists integers, booleans and JSON-text columns; monetary integers are cents, with document source currency preserved.
  3. Map the literal \N token to null before any other conversion; empty text stays empty. Then remove exactly one leading transport apostrophe from text columns. The schema records both sets of cell coordinates for audit. Keep the original JSON model for exact source evidence. CSV escaping is not a universal spreadsheet safety guarantee.
  4. Use the declared parent keys and relationships. Reconcile posted = unpaid + paid and count distinct document IDs. Keep unmatched references in review; do not join financial facts directly or add the financial stages.

The optional file handoff does not change the simulation. All model and dashboard interactions run in this browser; no external analysis application is required. Microsoft Text/CSV import guidance · Microsoft relationship guidance

Measure definitions

Values are net USD in this simulation. Received-not-invoiced is within open commitment. Posted invoices = unpaid + paid. Do not add these stages as separate purchases.

Checks on this checkpoint

Passed means the inspected rows satisfy this check. Empty means no rows were available to test. Held identifies a review condition, not a guessed correction.

    How the demonstrations are built.

    HTML, CSS, JavaScript and a shared source of truth

    Semantic HTML supplies the page structure and native navigation. CSS supplies the responsive layouts and shared light/dark palette. JavaScript rule modules enforce policy, replay commands, validate checkpoints and project the analytical model; separate view modules render those results. Public portfolio pages are generated from the canonical simulations and checked for drift.

    The financial model is computed from the selected purchasing journal. Example checkpoints replay the same workflow commands as the demonstration. Choosing an example here does not replace saved progress. Browser storage illustrates recovery on this device; role selectors illustrate responsibilities, not authenticated access control.

    Preventing double counts and misleading totals

    Approved PO lines relate separately to cost allocations and invoice-line allocations. Invoice documents relate to their allocations, current reasons and evaluation history. Joining two facts directly can multiply rows. Keep each measure at its own grain, aggregate before combining results, and count distinct document IDs for invoices. The dictionary and record inspector show those boundaries.

    Amounts use integer cents. Allocation rounding reconciles to the original line. Unsupported currencies and unresolved references remain visible as holds. The report does not invent exchange rates or infer an expense account from the vendor alone.

    Historical research is a separate source

    The attributed BPI Challenge 2019 purchase-order event log supports a separate historical process analysis. Its event counts and timelines are not joined to this fictional company, and its amounts are not used to manufacture company savings. Open the historical source, transformations and license.

    What a production implementation would add

    This is a simulated presentation. A production system would need approved source-system integration, authenticated identities, enforced permissions, durable shared storage, managed secrets, deployment ownership and operational monitoring. The current browser report is implemented in HTML, CSS and JavaScript; it is not an embedded Power BI report, live ERP connection, live SCADA controller or invoice OCR service.
